s0003.literal: Shen Jiong; Yu Li; younger brother Ji; Ma Shu
s0003.idiomatic: Shen Jiong; Yu Li; younger brother Ji; Ma Shu

s0004.literal: Shen Jiong, styled Liming, Editorial footnote marker 1. was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.
s0004.idiomatic: Shen Jiong, styled Liming, [1] came from Wukang in Wuxing.

s0005.literal: His grandfather Yu was Administrator of Xunyang under Liang.
s0005.idiomatic: His grandfather Yu had been Liang's administrator of Xunyang.

s0006.literal: His father Xu was a staff recorder in a princely establishment.
s0006.idiomatic: His father Xu was a recorder on a prince's staff.

s0007.literal: Jiong in youth had outstanding talent and was esteemed by his age.
s0007.idiomatic: Jiong showed rare talent in youth and was held in esteem.

s0008.literal: He doffed the commoner's garb as a kingdom regular attendant, was transferred to be Vice Minister of the Left for the People in the Secretariat, and went out as magistrate of Wu.
s0008.idiomatic: He entered service as a kingdom regular attendant, rose to vice minister of the left for the people, and was posted as magistrate of Wu.

s0009.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion the Administrator of Wu commandery Yuan Junzheng entered to relieve the capital and made Jiong overseer of the commandery.
s0009.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion Yuan Junzheng, administrator of Wu, marched to relieve the capital and left Jiong to oversee the commandery.

s0010.literal: When the capital fell, Jing's general Song Zixian held Wuxing and sent an envoy to summon Jiong, entrusting him with secretarial duties.
s0010.idiomatic: The capital fell. Jing's general Song Zixian held Wuxing and summoned Jiong to keep his records.

s0011.literal: Jiong firmly declined on grounds of illness; Zixian was enraged and ordered him beheaded.
s0011.idiomatic: Jiong pleaded illness and refused. Zixian flew into a rage and ordered his execution.

s0012.literal: Jiong removed his robe to await the blade; he was hindered by a mulberry tree in the road, was then dragged elsewhere, and someone hastily rescued him—he barely escaped.
s0012.idiomatic: He stripped for the blade, but a mulberry in the road blocked the stroke. They dragged him elsewhere; someone rushed to save him, and he barely lived.

s0013.literal: Zixian loved his talent and in the end forced him to take charge of secretarial work.
s0013.idiomatic: Zixian prized his gift for words and at last compelled him to keep the records.

s0014.literal: When Zixian was defeated by Wang Sengbian, Sengbian had long heard his name and in the army ransomed him, rewarding the captor with one hundred thousand iron coins; from then on urgent dispatches and military documents all came from Jiong's hand.
s0014.idiomatic: When Zixian fell to Wang Sengbian, Sengbian, who had long known his name, bought him out of the ranks for one hundred thousand iron coins. After that every dispatch and army paper bore Jiong's hand.

s0015.literal: When Emperor Jianwen of Liang was killed, territorial governors everywhere sent memorials to Jiangling urging enthronement; Sengbian had Jiong draft the memorial—the writing was very skilled, and none of the time could match it.
s0015.idiomatic: After Emperor Jianwen was killed, governors everywhere sent memorials to Jiangling urging a new throne. Sengbian had Jiong draft them. None of the age could match his craft.

s0016.literal: When the Founder marched south and met Sengbian at Baimao Bay, they ascended the altar and set the covenant; Jiong wrote its text.
s0016.idiomatic: When the Founder marched south he met Sengbian at Baimao Bay. They mounted the altar and swore alliance; Jiong wrote the words.

s0017.literal: When Hou Jing fled east to Wu commandery he seized Jiong's wife, née Yu, and his son Xingjian, and killed them both; Jiong's younger brother carried off their mother and escaped.
s0017.idiomatic: When Hou Jing fled east into Wu commandery he seized Jiong's wife, Lady Yu, and his son Xingjian and killed them. Jiong's younger brother fled with their mother and lived.

s0018.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified, Emperor Yuan of Liang pitied that his wife and children had died in the slaughter and specially enfeoffed him as Marquis of Yuanxiang with a fief of five hundred households.
s0018.idiomatic: After Hou Jing fell, Emperor Yuan of Liang pitied the slaughter of his household and specially enfeoffed him as Marquis of Yuanxiang with five hundred households.

s0019.literal: When Sengbian became Minister of Education, he made Jiong a retainer in his secretariat.
s0019.idiomatic: When Sengbian became minister of education he made Jiong a secretariat retainer.

s0020.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang summoned him as Attendant of the Yellow Gate in the Secretariat and concurrent Left Director of the Secretariat.
s0020.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan summoned him as attendant of the yellow gate and concurrent left director of the Secretariat.

s0021.literal: When Jingzhou fell he was captured by Western Wei; the Wei people treated him with great courtesy and appointed Jiong Palace Attendant of the Third Rank.
s0021.idiomatic: When Jingzhou fell he was taken by Western Wei. They honored him and made him palace attendant of the third rank.

s0022.literal: Because his mother was old in the east, Jiong constantly longed to return home, fearing the Wei would love his literary talent and detain him; he always shut his gate and swept no visitors, having no social ties.
s0022.idiomatic: His mother was old in the east and he longed to go home, fearing the Wei would keep him for his writing. He shut his gate, swept away callers, and kept no company.

s0023.literal: Whenever he had writings he at once destroyed them and would not let them circulate.
s0023.idiomatic: Whatever he wrote he destroyed at once and would not let it spread.

s0024.literal: Once, walking alone past Emperor Wu of Han's Tower of Reaching Heaven, he submitted a memorial stating his wish to return.
s0024.idiomatic: Once he walked alone past the Han Tower of Reaching Heaven and submitted a memorial pleading to return.

s0025.literal: The text says: "Your servant has heard that though Qiao Mountain is covered over, the spirit of the Tripod Lake may still be worshipped; though Youlu is waste, the traces of the Great Court are not lost.
s0025.idiomatic: He wrote: "I have heard that though Qiao Mountain is buried, the spirit at Tripod Lake may still be honored; though Youlu lies waste, the Great Court's traces are not gone.

s0026.literal: I bow before Your Majesty's descending virtue like the orchid on the slope, your gathering of numinous power in the rich valley.
s0026.idiomatic: I bow before Your Majesty's grace descending like orchids on the slope, your gathering of numinous power in the rich valley.

s0027.literal: When Han's Way had ascended, immortals could be hoped for; shooting the zhi at the sea shore, performing rites at Sun Terrace and proclaiming merit, crossing midstream on the Fen River, pointing to Cypress Beam and feasting high—what joy, is it not so!
s0027.idiomatic: When Han's Way had risen, immortals seemed near: shooting zhi at the sea shore, rites at Sun Terrace proclaiming merit, crossing midstream on the Fen, feasting high at Cypress Beam—what joy, was it not so!

s0028.literal: Then fortune turned to the transcendent lord, the Way reached the imperial carriage's halt; armored curtains and pearl blinds fell in a morning; the jade bowl of Maoling came forth among men; the old base of Lingyun shared the open fields in lush growth; the separate wind's remnant
s0028.idiomatic: Then fate turned to the transcendent lord and the imperial carriage halted; armored curtains and pearl blinds fell in a morning; Maoling's jade bowl walked among men; Lingyun's old base turned to lush open fields; the remnant of the separate wind

s0030.literal: [site], Editorial footnote marker 2. facing the tomb mound in boundless expanse—a captive minister in bonds, how could he not shed tears?
s0030.idiomatic: [site], [2] facing the tomb mounds in boundless haze—a captive minister in bonds, how could tears not fall?

s0031.literal: In old days when Chenming was weary, Yan Zhu returned east; four-horse carriages could be taken, Sima Xiangru came back west—I respectfully hear these precedents and secretly harbor this foolish wish.
s0031.idiomatic: When Chenming grew weary, Yan Zhu went east; four-horse carriages waited, Sima Xiangru returned west—I hear these precedents and harbor this foolish wish.

s0032.literal: Though millet and millet are not fragrant, I dare not forget to seek blessing.
s0032.idiomatic: Though the offering lacks fragrance, I dare not forget to seek blessing.

s0033.literal: " When the memorial was finished, that night Jiong dreamed of a place within the palace precincts where guards were very strict; he stated his case, and heard someone say: "We are quite willing to let you return—when may you arrive?"
s0033.idiomatic: " When the memorial was done, that night he dreamed of palace precincts under strict guard. He pleaded his case and heard a voice: "We are quite willing to let you go home—when will you arrive?"

s0034.literal: " Within a few days he and Wang Ke and others were all able to return east.
s0034.idiomatic: " Within days he and Wang Ke and others were all sent home to the east.

s0035.literal: In the second year of Shaotai he reached the capital and was made Director of the Directorate of Agriculture, then transferred to Censor-in-Chief.
s0035.idiomatic: In Shaotai year 2 (555) he reached the capital, was made director of the directorate of agriculture, then censor-in-chief.

s0036.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, Jiong was given the added post of Regular Attendant for Direct Communication, censor-in-chief unchanged.
s0036.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne he was given the added post of regular attendant for direct communication while keeping the censorate.

s0037.literal: Because his mother was old he memorialized asking to return and support her; an edict did not permit it.
s0037.idiomatic: He memorialized to go home and tend his aged mother; the court refused.

s0038.literal: When Emperor Wen succeeded he again memorialized, saying: "Your servant from infancy met misfortune; at twenty he was orphaned; mother and son were alone, brothers raised one another.
s0038.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen succeeded he memorialized again: "From infancy I met misfortune. At twenty I was orphaned; mother and son were alone, brothers raised each other.

s0039.literal: I kept my person to support them, took office without choosing rank, served to completion under Liang, my life preserved in chaotic times, braving danger and treading peril,
s0039.idiomatic: I kept my body to nourish them, took any office, served Liang to the end, and lived through chaos, braving danger at every step,

s0041.literal: [hundred] deaths counted light, Editorial footnote marker 3. wife and children executed, brothers extinguished; your servant and his mother alone met the rising fortune.
s0041.idiomatic: [hundred] deaths counted light, [3] wife and children slain, brothers gone; only your servant and his mother met this rising fortune.

s0042.literal: Your servant's mother, concubine Liu, is this year eighty-one; your servant's uncle's wife, concubine Qiu, is seventy-five; your servant's younger brothers and nephews in the clan are gone, and concubine Qiu's grandsons long since perished—of the two households to be served, only your servant remains.
s0042.idiomatic: My mother, Lady Liu, is eighty-one; my uncle's wife, Lady Qiu, is seventy-five. Our younger kin are gone and Lady Qiu's grandsons are long dead—of the two households that must be served, only I remain.

s0043.literal: The former emperor knew your servant's loneliness, nourished him with a post in his home district, and did not wish him to dwell suddenly in the wilds; he again pitied your servant's warmth in winter and cool in summer, so within one year he granted leave again and again.
s0043.idiomatic: The late emperor knew my desolation, kept me in a post near home, and would not leave me in the wild; he pitied my duty to warm and cool my elders, and within a year granted leave again and again.

s0044.literal: Your servant's repeated laying bare of his loyal heart and frequent braving of the imperial gaze were not from wishing to defy the court or leave the capital region.
s0044.idiomatic: I laid my heart bare again and again and braved the throne's gaze—not because I wished to defy the court or flee the capital.

s0045.literal: First, as the years approach sixty, boiling water sits in the heart; whenever kneeling to read a letter from home, fear comes before and joy after; warming the pillow and fanning the mat—no longer the ways of childhood.
s0045.idiomatic: First, nearing sixty, my heart is scalding water; each time I kneel to a letter from home, fear comes first and joy after; to warm the pillow and fan the mat is no longer the work of a child.

s0046.literal: Second, the office holds the imperial statutes—the state's straightedge; if one himself impairs the rites of the body, Editorial footnote marker 4. how may one inquire into the nation's laws?
s0046.idiomatic: Second, my post holds the imperial statutes—the state's straightedge; if I impair my own filial duty, [4] how may I judge the nation's laws?

s0047.literal: Former grace was close and at first allowed compassionate release; inner attendants and close ministers mostly knew this intent.
s0047.idiomatic: Former grace was close and at first promised compassionate release; inner attendants and close ministers knew that intent.

s0048.literal: It was only because in choosing the worthy and employing the able, widely seeking the wise and clear, I hesitated and delayed and had not yet taken talent.
s0048.idiomatic: Only because in choosing the worthy and seeking the wise I hesitated and delayed, and had not yet yielded my post.

s0049.literal: Yet High Heaven sent down affliction and suddenly it reached today; the virtuous voice is still in the ear, the grave earth is already dry—vast is August Heaven, pity this boundless grief.
s0049.idiomatic: Yet Heaven sent down affliction and suddenly it is today; his gracious voice is still in my ear, the grave earth already dry—vast Heaven, pity this boundless grief.

s0050.literal: Together with your servant's private heart seared and pressed, ever nearer in time, his earnest prayer forgets even dust on his robe.
s0050.idiomatic: Together with my private heart seared and pressed, ever nearer in time, earnest prayer forgets even the dust on my robe.

s0051.literal: I bow before Your Majesty's wise clarity and intelligence, succeeding and raising martial virtue, taking punishment as model for the four seas and spreading this filial governance.
s0051.idiomatic: I bow before Your Majesty's wise clarity, raising martial virtue in succession, taking punishment as model for the four seas and spreading this filial rule.

s0052.literal: With an inch of brush I seek Heaven, looking up to return within the curtain; where there is feeling there must be response—I truly look to sagely clarity.
s0052.idiomatic: With an inch of brush I seek Heaven, looking up to return within the curtain; where feeling moves, response must come—I trust in sagely clarity.

s0053.literal: I specially beg that you grant in full my private rites; then the kingly virtue will reach without limit—how much more those who soar and sink, who are not all nurtured?
s0053.idiomatic: I beg that you grant my private rites in full; then kingly virtue reaches without limit—how much more those who soar and sink, who are not all nurtured?

s0054.literal: " The edict replied: "I have read your memorial and take your meaning.
s0054.idiomatic: " The edict replied: "Your memorial is received and your meaning understood.

s0055.literal: Your fame has raced through Xianyang and Luoyang; your feeling runs deep as Wan and Pei.
s0055.idiomatic: Your fame has raced through Xianyang and Luoyang; your feeling runs deep as Wan and Pei.

s0056.literal: Lately reason pressed at the leaning door, Editorial footnote marker 5. words turned toward a foreign land; again bound by timely service, you missed attending them.
s0056.idiomatic: Lately reason pressed at the leaning door, [5] words turned toward a foreign land; again bound by timely service, you missed attending them.

s0057.literal: Though Zhou Sheng's thought each time wished to abandon office, Dai Li's handed-down text allowed leaving office to follow policy; the former court's glory filled the four seas and toiled at the myriad affairs of state—because your talent stood alone, your office held the special mat, and just as deep trust was placed, again and again feeling and rites were bent.
s0057.idiomatic: Though Zhou Sheng's thought each time wished to quit office, Dai Li's handed-down text allowed leaving office for policy; the former court's glory filled the four seas and toiled at myriad affairs—because your talent stood alone, your office held the special mat, and just as trust deepened, again and again feeling and rites were bent.

s0058.literal: I now succeed to the great foundation, thinking to spread the splendid enterprise; looking on this meager thinness and also wound with mourning grief, I truly rely on the worthy and wise to bring harmony together—how could I lightly set aside the southern ministries and unfasten the eastern road?
s0058.idiomatic: I now succeed to the great foundation and think to spread the splendid enterprise; looking on my meager worth and wound with mourning, I truly rely on the worthy to bring harmony—how could I lightly set aside the southern ministries and unfasten the eastern road?

s0059.literal: Today Feng Qin entered the house and Xun's mother followed the office—you may see court glory without impairing family rites.
s0059.idiomatic: Today Feng Qin entered the house and Xun's mother followed the office—you may see court glory without impairing family rites.

s0060.literal: Soon I shall order the responsible offices to welcome your honored kin, so that you may have what is fitting in public and private, and nothing will be neglected."
s0060.idiomatic: Soon I shall order the responsible offices to welcome your honored kin, so that public and private needs are met, and nothing neglected."

s0061.literal: Earlier the Founder had said Jiong was fit for a king's assistant; in great affairs of army and state he took part in many plans; Emperor Wen again valued his talent and wished to honor him richly.
s0061.idiomatic: Earlier the Founder had said Jiong was fit for a king's assistant; in army and state he took part in many plans; Emperor Wen again valued his talent and wished to honor him richly.

s0062.literal: It happened that Wang Lin invaded Dalei and Liu Yi held the eastern marches; the emperor wished to have Jiong win merit thereby, so relieved him as censor-in-chief, gave him the added title General of Bright Prestige, and sent him back to his home district to gather followers.
s0062.idiomatic: When Wang Lin invaded Dalei and Liu Yi held the eastern marches, the emperor wished Jiong to win merit thereby, relieved him as censor-in-chief, made him general of bright prestige, and sent him home to gather followers.

s0063.literal: He died of illness in Wu, aged fifty-nine.
s0063.idiomatic: He died of illness in Wu, aged fifty-nine.

s0064.literal: When Emperor Wen heard it he at once went into mourning and also sent condolences; he was posthumously made Palace Attendant, posthumous name Gongzi.
s0064.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen heard it he mourned that same day and sent condolences; he was posthumously made palace attendant, posthumous name Gongzi.

s0065.literal: He had a collected works in twenty rolls circulating in the world.
s0065.idiomatic: A collected works in twenty rolls circulated in his time.

s0066.literal: Yu Li, styled Shanpi, was a native of Yuyao in Kuaiji.
s0066.idiomatic: Yu Li, styled Shanpi, came from Yuyao in Kuaiji.

s0067.literal: His grandfather Quan was Minister of Justice under Liang and Administrator of Yongjia.
s0067.idiomatic: His grandfather Quan was Liang's minister of justice and administrator of Yongjia.

s0068.literal: His father Jian was a staff adviser to the Prince of Shixing, Pacifier of the North.
s0068.idiomatic: His father Jian was a staff adviser to the Prince of Shixing, pacifier of the north.

s0069.literal: Li in youth was clever and keen, with will and conduct.
s0069.idiomatic: Li was clever and keen in youth, with firm will and conduct.

s0070.literal: At age nine he followed his father's elder brother Kan to call on the Minister of Rites Lu Yan; Yan asked ten matters on the Five Classics and Li answered each question as asked, missing nothing—Yan marveled at him.
s0070.idiomatic: At nine he followed his father's elder brother Kan to call on Minister of Rites Lu Yan. Yan asked ten points on the Five Classics; Li answered each without miss, and Yan marveled.

s0071.literal: He also once visited the recluse He Yin; at the time the Administrator, the Prince of Hengyang, also came, and Yin spoke of him to the prince; the prince wished to see Li, but Li declined, saying: "I have no visiting tablet and cannot pay respects.
s0071.idiomatic: He once visited the recluse He Yin. The Prince of Hengyang, then administrator, also came; Yin spoke of Li to the prince, who wished to see him. Li declined: "I have no visiting tablet and cannot pay respects.

s0072.literal: " The prince, because Li had lofty aims, honored him deeply; returning to his commandery he at once summoned him as chief clerk, but Li again declined on grounds of youth and did not accept.
s0072.idiomatic: " The prince, seeing Li's lofty aims, honored him deeply. Back in his commandery he summoned Li as chief clerk; Li again declined as too young.

s0073.literal: When grown he had fine bearing, broadly read the classics, and was skilled at literary composition.
s0073.idiomatic: Grown, he had fine bearing, read broadly in the classics, and wrote well.

s0074.literal: He doffed the commoner's garb as a traveling aide in Liang's Western Central Commandery, soon was appointed Outer Army Major in the Law Office, and concurrently Chief of the Danyang Imperial Prison.
s0074.idiomatic: He entered service as a traveling aide in Liang's western central commandery, soon as outer-army major in the law office and concurrent chief of the Danyang imperial prison.

s0075.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang set up the Forest of Scholars Hall west of the city; Li composed a stele, submitted it, and the emperor ordered it carved in the hall and still employed Li as a Forest of Scholars academician.
s0075.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang set up the Forest of Scholars west of the city. Li composed a stele and submitted it; the emperor had it carved in the hall and made Li an academician there.

s0076.literal: Soon he was made Editorial Officer of Writings, transferred to Regular Attendant for Direct Communication, and concurrently Secretariat Gentleman.
s0076.idiomatic: Soon he was editorial officer of writings, then regular attendant for direct communication and concurrent secretariat gentleman.

s0077.literal: At the time those in close attendance mostly shared in the power axis; inner and outer affairs were each partly held—only Li and Gu Xie were calm, retiring, and dwelt in the Western Secretariat, known only through literature and history; the age called them pure.
s0077.idiomatic: Close attendants then mostly shared the power axis; inner and outer affairs were split among them—only Li and Gu Xie stayed calm and retired in the western secretariat, known for literature and history; the age called them pure.

s0078.literal: Soon he headed the Grand Institute for Writing.
s0078.idiomatic: Soon he headed the grand institute for writing.

s0079.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, Li led kin into the Terrace City and was made Staff Adviser to the Pacifier of the West, secretariat gentleman unchanged.
s0079.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled Li led kin into the Terrace City and was made staff adviser to the pacifier of the west, secretariat gentleman unchanged.

s0080.literal: When the Terrace City fell he fled home.
s0080.idiomatic: When the Terrace City fell he fled home.

s0081.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified, Emperor Yuan summoned him as Secretariat Gentleman and Marquis of Zhenyang, and appointed him Vice Governor of Yangzhou—all of which he did not accept.
s0081.idiomatic: When Hou Jing fell, Emperor Yuan summoned him as secretariat gentleman and Marquis of Zhenyang and made him vice governor of Yangzhou; he accepted none of it.

s0082.literal: When Zhang Biao held Kuaiji, Li was there.
s0082.idiomatic: When Zhang Biao held Kuaiji, Li was there.

s0083.literal: When Emperor Wen pacified Biao, the Founder sent Li a letter saying: "Since the mourning and chaos, worthies have scattered; your talent and use are fine, your fame heard in Xu and Luo; today's court is newly ordered and widely seeks heroes—how can you linger in the eastern lands and keep goodness to yourself?
s0083.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen pacified Biao, the Founder wrote: "Since the chaos, worthies have scattered. Your talent is fine and your fame heard in Xu and Luo. The court is newly ordered and seeks heroes widely—how can you linger in the east and keep goodness to yourself?

s0084.literal: I now order your elder brother's son to come out and meet you in the capital; surely you will answer the court's eager waiting.
s0084.idiomatic: I now order your elder brother's son to bring you to the capital; surely you will answer the court's eager waiting.

s0085.literal: " Emperor Wen also wrote: "You have beauty in the southeast, fame that spreads; you should yourself brush the capital and Xu, together set right the age's ills, yet
s0085.idiomatic: " Emperor Wen also wrote: "You have beauty in the southeast and fame that spreads; you should brush the capital and Xu and set right the age's ills, yet

s0087.literal: [pared] your traces in gardens and fields, Editorial footnote marker 6. keeping this solitary goodness—will you let the empty valley's hope be spoken in vain?
s0087.idiomatic: [pared] your traces in gardens and fields, [6] keeping solitary goodness—will you let the empty valley's hope be spoken in vain?

s0088.literal: I surely wish you at once to pack and also make plans to leave for the capital.
s0088.idiomatic: I surely wish you to pack at once and plan to leave for the capital.

s0089.literal: I only wait to see you—may that day be soon.
s0089.idiomatic: I only wait to see you—may that day be soon.

s0090.literal: " Pressed urgently and with no way out, he then answered the summons and reached the capital.
s0090.idiomatic: " Pressed urgently and with no way out, he answered the summons and reached the capital.

s0091.literal: When the Founder died and Emperor Wen succeeded, Li was made Crown Prince Attendant and still attended the crown prince in study.
s0091.idiomatic: When the Founder died and Emperor Wen succeeded, Li was made crown prince attendant and still tutored the crown prince.

s0092.literal: Soon he headed the Grand Institute for Writing and was Grand Arbiter for the two provinces of East Yang and Yangzhou, attendant unchanged.
s0092.idiomatic: Soon he headed the grand institute for writing and was grand arbiter for East Yang and Yangzhou, attendant unchanged.

s0093.literal: Earlier Li's mother had followed Li into the Terrace City and died within it; soon the city fell and feeling and rites could not be observed—therefore for life he ate vegetables and wore plain cloth, heard no music; though his appointment was weighty, his dwelling was spare and he had no designs.
s0093.idiomatic: Earlier his mother had followed him into the Terrace City and died there; soon the city fell and rites could not be observed—therefore for life he ate vegetables and plain cloth and heard no music; though honored in office, his dwelling was spare and he had no designs.

s0094.literal: Emperor Wen valued him deeply, constantly kept him at hand, and morning and evening sought his counsel.
s0094.idiomatic: Emperor Wen valued him deeply, kept him at hand, and morning and evening sought his counsel.

s0095.literal: Li by nature was deep and close, seldom spoke in debate; whatever he offered in counsel, none saw its inner workings—therefore he is not listed in what follows.
s0095.idiomatic: Li by nature was deep and close, seldom debated; whatever he offered in counsel none saw its inner workings—therefore he is not listed in what follows.

s0096.literal: At the time Li's second younger brother Ji was staying in Min, relying on Chen Baoying; whenever Li spoke of it he wept.
s0096.idiomatic: At the time Li's second younger brother Ji was staying in Min under Chen Baoying; whenever Li spoke of it he wept.

s0097.literal: Emperor Wen pitied him and said: "I too have a brother far away; this feeling is very keen—how would others know?
s0097.idiomatic: Emperor Wen pitied him and said: "I too have a brother far away; this feeling is keen—how would others know?

s0098.literal: " He then ordered Baoying to send Ji back, but Baoying in the end did not send him.
s0098.idiomatic: " He then ordered Baoying to send Ji back, but Baoying never sent him.

s0099.literal: Li thereby fell ill with grief; the emperor several times went in person to visit him.
s0099.idiomatic: Li fell ill with grief; the emperor visited him in person several times.

s0100.literal: He ordered Li to bring his household into the Secretariat; Li said the forbidden precinct was no private dwelling and begged to stop outside the walls; Emperor Wen did not permit it and had him stay at Orchid Terrace; the imperial carriage again and again visited him in person; hand-edicts and inner envoys lined the road.
s0100.idiomatic: He ordered Li to bring his household into the secretariat; Li said the forbidden precinct was no private home and begged to stay outside the walls. Emperor Wen refused and had him stay at Orchid Terrace; the imperial carriage visited again and again; hand-edicts and inner envoys lined the road.
